originality.rationale: The finite-lag OU coefficients are explicitly older (Lade 2009) and generic Pearson Student tails and moment dynamics are explicitly older (Monthus 2023 and Forman–Sørensen 2008). The final claim adds the global one-peak sampling-lag growth profile and the resulting reentrant discounted quartic finiteness interval at fixed discount; these are absent from the closely inspected primary literature. No equivalent published record was found by the stated queries. Priority uncertainty from possible recombination or alternative vocabulary remains.

value.rationale: Fourth-order polynomial evaluation is the first even-degree test that exposes the mismatch between perfectly matched second stationary moments and heavy-tail moment failure. The rigorous bounded intermediate sampling-lag singular band with recovery of discounted integrability at very large lag is not a routine single-parameter substitution: it yields a global nonmonotone phase diagram and a practical stability diagnostic for uncentered-increment-based continuous-time policy evaluation. No new universal algorithm performance guarantee is asserted.
